item.title: Rupture and far-field profiles for H\'enon-type MEMS elliptic equation with pressure
item.description: arXiv:2611.31349v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by membrane touchdown in electrostatic microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) under external pressure, we study the H\'enon-type elliptic equation $\Delta u=\lambda|x|^{\alpha}u^{-p}+F$, $u>0$, where $N\ge2$, $\lambda,p>0$, $\alpha>-2$, $F\in\mathbb R$, and $\alpha<2p$ if $F\ne0$. Near the origin, we construct positive radial rupture solutions with $u(0)=0$ for $F\ne0$ and infinitely many non-radial but asymptotically radial ones for every $F$, and derive expansions to arbitrary order. On exterior domains $\Omega_{R_0}:=\{x\in\mathbb R^N:|x|>R_0\}$, with no condition at the origin, we establish existence and uniqueness of positive solutions on $[R_0,\infty)$ for radial initial value problems with $u(R_0)>0$ if $p\ge1$, or if $F\ge0$ and $u'(R_0)\ge0$. We determine the leading behavior of all positive radial exterior solutions as $|x|\to\infty$ for $F>0$ and $F=0$, and for $F<0$ when $p\ge1$ and $\alpha\ge0$. For possibly non-radial exterior solutions satisfying $u(r,\theta)=A_\infty r^{\sigma_\infty}(1+o(1))$ uniformly in $\theta$, with $A_\infty>0$ and $\sigma_\infty\in\mathbb R$, we uniquely determine the leading exponent and coefficient in all three pressure regimes, without derivative bounds on the remainder. Although pressure affects only higher-order terms near an asymptotically radial rupture point, its sign changes the leading-order behavior at infinity under the stated hypotheses. Local radial rupture solutions extend uniquely to $\mathbb R^N\setminus\{0\}$ for $F>0$, and for $F<0$ when $p\ge1$, with the classified far-field profiles under the corresponding hypotheses.
item.dc:creator: Yunxiao Li, Yanyan Zhang

item.title: Localization and homogenization of anisotropic fractional energies
item.description: arXiv:2611.31416v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the joint limit of localization ($s\uparrow1$) and periodic homogenization ($\varepsilon\downarrow0$) for anisotropic fractional energies with $p$-growth and oscillating kernels. We prove that the $\Gamma$-limit is governed by the single parameter $\theta=\lim\varepsilon^{p(1-s)}$, and that its density is the convex combination $\theta\mathcal{A}^* + (1-\theta)\bar{\mathcal{A}}$ of the homogenized and the averaged densities. This shows that the picture recently obtained for quadratic energies also holds for every $p$ and for anisotropic kernels, with no regularity in the oscillating variable; the approach is different, and is based on convex duality. A nonlocal version of the duality argument gives the limit as $s\uparrow 1$ for a fixed kernel under weak assumptions, correcting a previous proof by the authors.
item.dc:creator: Juli\'an Fern\'andez Bonder, Ariel Salort

item.title: Exterior $p$-capacitary rigidity on groups of Heisenberg type
item.description: arXiv:2611.31493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the exterior Bernoulli overdetermined problem for sub-elliptic operators. Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a group of Heisenberg type with Property (H), and let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{G}$ be a domain enjoying a partial symmetry property and containing a Kor\'{a}nyi-Kaplan ball $\overline{B_r}$ centered at the origin. We consider a function $u$ that is $p$-harmonic with respect to the $p$-sub-Laplacian $\Delta_{\mathbb{G},p}$ in the annular region $\Omega \setminus \overline{B}_r$, satisfying the boundary conditions $ u = 0 \;\text{ on }\; \partial\Omega, \quad u = 1 \;\text{ on }\; \partial B_r.$ We show that if $p$ is even and $u$ satisfies a mild overdetermined condition on the sub-Riemannian norm of its gradient on the outer boundary $\partial\Omega$, then $\Omega$ must itself be a Kor\'{a}nyi--Kaplan ball centered at the origin, and $u$ is the corresponding normalized capacitary potential; equivalently, away from the pole it is an affine normalization of the fundamental solution of $\Delta_{\mathbb{G},p}$.
item.dc:creator: Federica Dragoni, Nicola Garofalo, Gianmarco Giovannardi, Paolo Salani, Dimiter Vassilev

item.title: Airy Path Integral Representation for the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili Equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.31500v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a representation for solutions of the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili II (KP-II) equation as path integrals over the Airy line ensemble. The initial condition enters directly as a potential, bypassing the usual direct and inverse scattering constructions. We establish the representation for broad classes of signed initial data, prove uniqueness in specified solution classes, and derive a restart identity expressing solutions as Airy path integrals of their own earlier states. For arbitrary real $L^2$ initial data, a centered version of the Airy occupation represents the standard global KP-II flow. We show how the representation recovers the classical Marchenko determinant for Korteweg-de Vries (KdV), and identify a Brownian-path amplitude with the classical KP-II heat-scattering coefficient. We obtain explicit formulas for soliton solutions and derive KP from a Toda equation for nonintersecting Brownian bridges. Finally, we use the restart identity to characterize one-point distributions of the KPZ fixed point through their singular initial conditions, and derive sharp lower-tail asymptotics directly from KP.
item.dc:creator: Jeremy Quastel, C. Alexander Rodriguez

item.title: Local Reynolds number criteria for the regularity of the three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations, and their consistency with forced finite-time blow-up
item.description:
arXiv:2611.31565v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give four regularity criteria for the forced Navier-Stokes equations in $\mathbb{R}^3$. The first is an $\dot H^1$ estimate: a strong solution cannot blow up while the local Reynolds number $|v|^2/(
u|\omega|)$ stays below $4/(3\sqrt3)$ wherever the vorticity exceeds a threshold $M(t)$ with $\int M^{6/5}\,dt<\infty$. It rests on an exact identity that gives the cubic vorticity term a favorable sign. Two further $\dot H^1$ estimates use the Newton potential of $|\omega|^2$, either as a multiplier or as a gradient added to the Lamb vector, so that the integral of $|\omega|^2|v|^2$ cancels. The second of these gives a critical condition on the vorticity alone, implied by $\int\|\omega\|_{L^3}^2\,dt<\infty$. The fourth is a maximum principle for $ rac12|v|^2+\lambda|\omega|$: vortex stretching is absorbed by viscous dissipation, and the pressure is controlled by a weighted local estimate. It requires a bound on $|v|^2/(
u|
abla v|)$ only at maximum points where the velocity part dominates. We show that the forced finite-time blow-up recently constructed by OpenAI violates each hypothesis, and that the violations locate its mechanism: inflow down the centripetal pressure gradient, at the same order as viscous dissipation.
item.dc:creator: Ali Bouzekri

item.title: Inviscid limit of steady Navier--Stokes equations with Navier friction boundary conditions in a periodic channel
item.description: arXiv:2611.31652v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The vanishing viscosity limit of the steady incompressible Navier--Stokes equations is studied in a periodic channel with Navier friction boundary conditions, where the slip length is assumed to be a nonnegative power of the viscosity. Depending on this power, the problem falls into subcritical, critical, and supercritical regimes. In each regime, the Navier--Stokes solutions are constructed via the Prandtl expansion, and the validity of the expansion is rigorously justified. By the Prandtl--Batchelor theory, the leading Euler solution is a Couette flow, and the interaction between the interior and boundary-layer profiles is precisely characterized. Of particular interest is the critical regime, in which the leading order Prandtl profile solves a nonlinear steady Prandtl equation with a Robin-type boundary condition. The well-posedness of this problem is established using the von Mises transformation and the implicit function theorem, and an implicit Batchelor--Wood formula is derived that determines the coefficients of the leading order Couette flow from the boundary data. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first well-posedness result for the steady Prandtl equation with a Robin-type boundary condition.
item.dc:creator: Robin Ming Chen, Dehua Wang, Weiqiang Wang

item.title: Classification of fast reaction limits for a two-component reaction-diffusion system
item.description: arXiv:2611.31697v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study fast reaction limits for a two-component reaction-diffusion system with four reaction exponents, in which only one component diffuses. For nonnegative segregated initial data, we classify the limits for all exponents at least one under homogeneous Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions. The limiting equations include the heat equation, a one-phase Stefan problem, a fixed-domain heat equation, and a nonlinear equation with a time-integral reaction term. We also describe the limiting behavior of the nondiffusing component and obtain a nontrivial rescaled limit. In the critical regime, we characterize the limit as the greatest weak solution and establish a transition between initial finite propagation and instantaneous positivity. Under Dirichlet conditions, permanent zero regions may occur for certain small initial data.
item.dc:creator: Yuki Tsukamoto

item.title: Variational Thresholds and Multiplicity for a Nonlocal r-Laplacian Logistic-Type Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.31701v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the existence, multiplicity and asymptotic behavior of solutions to a class of nonlocal logistic-type problems with the \(r\)-Laplacian operator in the fast diffusion regime: %, with a real parameter $\lambda$: \[ \begin{cases} -\Delta_r u - \displaystyle\int_{\Omega} K(x,y)u(y)\,dy = a(x)u +\lambda |u|^{q-2}u \displaystyle\int_\Omega Q(x,y)|u(y)|^q\,dy, & x\in \Omega, \\[0.4em] u = 0, & x\in \partial\Omega. \end{cases} \] The model has local diffusion, nonlocal dispersal, and nonlinear global interactions, and depends on a real parameter $\lambda$. For $\lambda \ge 0$, we establish the existence of nonnegative weak solutions via a variational principle. In the case \(\lambda<0\), we characterize two variational thresholds, \(-\infty<\widehat{\lambda}^*<\lambda^*<0\), which separate different solution intervals. For \(\lambda^*<\lambda<0\), the energy functional has a global minimizer with negative energy and a mountain-pass critical point with positive energy, yielding two distinct nontrivial weak solutions. The same holds at \(\lambda=\lambda^*\), where the global minimizer has zero energy. In a left neighborhood of \(\lambda^*\), two distinct nontrivial weak solutions persist, a local minimizer and a mountain-pass critical point, both with positive energy and the latter at a strictly higher level. For \(\lambda<\widehat{\lambda}^*\), only the trivial solution exists. Finally, as $\lambda \to 0^-$, the norm of the global minimizers blows up. Along subsequences, selected nonnegative mountain-pass solutions converge strongly in $W_0^{1,r}(\Omega)$ as $\lambda \to 0$ to a nontrivial nonnegative weak solution of the problem at $\lambda = 0$. The associated mountain-pass levels converge to the same limit from both sides of zero, and the corresponding solution norms also converge to a common value.
item.dc:creator: Thiago Cacau, Alireza Khatib

item.title: Modified wave operators for the critical long-range nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.31754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we construct modified wave operators for the critical long-range nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with final data $\langle x\rangle^s u_+\in L_x^2,\ d/2<s\le2$, for dimensions $d=1,2,3$, and for both defocusing and focusing cases. We impose no smallness, nonvanishing, or spatial derivative assumption. Most previous modified wave operator results require smallness on $\|\widehat u_+\|_{L^\infty}$, analytic final data or smooth amplitude-phase structure, and the large data modified wave operator problem with finite weighted condition is only solved for 1D defocusing equation. We introduce a new perturbation method which successfully applies to both defocusing and focusing signs when $d\le3$. The main ingredient is an improved growth estimate for the linearized flow, obtained by a low--high frequency decomposition. At low frequencies, spatial localization and freezing the coefficients in space lead to a Fuchsian system. The nilpotent structure at the singular point and a Hamiltonian energy estimate give logarithmic growth for this system. At high frequencies, a modified energy for suitable symmetry operator cancels the leading contribution to energy growth.
item.dc:creator: Jia Shen, Yifei Wu

item.title: Wiener-type criteria for parabolic equations with two-sided Gaussian bounds
item.description: arXiv:2611.31788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish sufficient and necessary Wiener-type criteria for boundary regularity of parabolic equations whose fundamental solutions satisfy two-sided Gaussian bounds. In particular, our sufficient criterion holds at the critical exponent in the Gaussian lower bound. For the heat equation, the resulting double-series criterion is equivalent to the classical Wiener criterion of Evans and Gariepy. Our results apply to divergence form equations with bounded measurable, possibly nonsymmetric coefficients, and to non-divergence form equations with coefficients in $\mathrm{DMO}_x$ (Dini mean oscillation in space), without requiring continuity in time.
item.dc:creator: Pilgyu Jung, Seick Kim, Sungjin Lee

item.title: Stokes corners and the global structure of steady rotating waves in annular domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.31808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study steady rotating water waves in a planar annulus, in the model of radial gravity and constant vorticity introduced by Li and the author. The stream function is harmonic, and the free surface carries the Bernoulli condition $p_0^2|\nabla\Psi|^2=Q_\alpha(S)$ with $Q_\alpha(R)=(R-r_-)(R-r_+)$. We first settle the crest shape. For $\alpha\neq\alpha_\pm$, every stagnation point lies on the circle $R=r_-$, and the surface forms a symmetric $120^\circ$ corner there. At $\alpha=\alpha_\pm$ the corner is a right angle. The same holds for limits of smooth solutions and, in the lower region, for overhanging waves. We then study the global bifurcation continuum. Its waves are monotone from crest to trough, and they always cross the laminar circle. Hence there is no secondary bifurcation, and the parameter stays above an explicit floor. The continuum ends in an extreme wave, overturns, or degenerates; the last case is excluded for $c_0>\gamma^2e^{2\gamma}/(1+\gamma)^2$. An annular Nekrasov equation and an invariant Keady--Norbury cone give a slope bound below $90^\circ$ whenever the Nekrasov weight is nonnegative on the waves. A sharpened angular flow-force estimate keeps the troughs where this weight is nonnegative, for every $\gamma\in(0,1)$ above the floor. Hence, whenever $c_0>\gamma^2e^{2\gamma}/(1+\gamma)^2$, the existence half of the Stokes conjecture holds: the continuum contains an extreme wave with a $120^\circ$ Stokes crest. In the remaining band $\sinh^2\gamma<c_0\le\gamma^2e^{2\gamma}/(1+\gamma)^2$ the result is conditional: the continuum ends in such a wave unless its parameter degenerates to the value at which the effective gravity vanishes on the stagnation circle, and we cannot exclude this degeneration. We also show that the bifurcation is supercritical for every $\gamma\in(0,1)$.
item.dc:creator: Quan Wang

item.title: Weighted pointwise estimates for the damped wave equation and global solutions to Nakao's problem in three dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.31881v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish weighted pointwise estimates for the Duhamel term of the three-dimensional damped wave equation. The estimates combine the parabolic weight $\langle t+|x|^2\rangle$ with the wave-cone weight $\langle t-|x|\rangle$, and thereby account for both the diffusive part of the damped wave flow and source terms with wave-like decay. As an application, we study Nakao's problem, a weakly coupled system consisting of one semilinear damped wave equation and one semilinear wave equation. Under explicit conditions on the exponents of nonlinear terms, we prove small-data global existence and uniqueness of mild solutions in weighted $L^\infty$ spaces. The result covers both the full parabolic decay and slower pointwise decay for the damped-wave component, and allows either the standard wave decay or slower pointwise decay for the wave component. The proof combines the new Duhamel estimate with weighted estimates for the free wave equation and a contraction argument.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Georgiev, Kosuke Kita

item.title: Uniform stabilization of degenerate thermoelasticity with non-autonomous conductivities
item.description: arXiv:2611.31907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a one-dimensional thermoelastic system with space- and time-dependent conductivity vanishing at one endpoint, under Dirichlet or zero-flux thermal conditions. Uniform comparison with the initial conductivity and local temporal regularity yield global well-posedness for energy data. A quadratic lower bound ensures uniform exponential decay for every fixed coupling $\kappa>0$, with constants depending only on $\kappa$ and uniform spatial bounds, independently of the starting time and local temporal regularity norms. This includes the critical conductivity $a=x^2$ with noncompact thermal embedding. For autonomous powers $a=x^\alpha$ with the corresponding boundary realizations, exponential stability holds uniformly in $\alpha$ for $0<\alpha\le2$. For $\alpha>2$, concentrating approximate equilibria show that the semigroup norm equals $1$ at every time and preclude uniform decay even from the generator graph domain to the energy space. Proofs combine a common-domain construction, interior-average compensation and time averaging for Dirichlet conditions, and a strict Lyapunov functional for zero-flux conditions.
item.dc:creator: Menglan Liao

item.title: On SQG Patches with $H^2$ Regularity
item.description: arXiv:2611.31923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study patch solutions of the generalized surface quasi-geostrophic (gSQG) equations, which is an interpolation between the 2D Euler ($\beta=0$) and the surface quasi-geostrophic (SQG) equations ($\beta=1$). We establish in the SQG case, the local well-posedness for patches with $H^2$ boundaries, which improves the previous result of $H^{2+s}$, $s>0$ by Gancedo--Nguyen--Patel \cite{Gancedo2022}. Also, in the gSQG case with $0<\beta<1$, the uniqueness of $H^2$ patch solutions is established. Our proofs are based on the contour dynamics formulation with constant speed, introduced in \cite{Gancedo2008}.
item.dc:creator: Shaoqing Chen, Yongzhong Sun

item.title: Wave interactions for the two-dimensional self-similar Euler equations of nonconvex gases
item.description: arXiv:2611.31980v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gases with nonconvex equations of state may differ significantly from polytropic ideal gases; for example, rarefaction and sonic shocks may occur. This paper studies a 2D Riemann initial-boundary value problem for the potential flow equations with a nonconvex equation of state. We construct global-in-time self-similar solutions by analyzing eight distinct types of wave interactions, including composite waves consisting of a sonic/double-sonic shock coupled with one or two fan waves. Three main difficulties arise in studying these wave interactions: the self-similar potential flow system is of mixed type, with its type at each point determined by the local pseudo-Mach number; the sonic or transonic nature of the shocks is not known a priori; and sonic singularities arise on sonic shocks. To overcome these difficulties, we proceed as follows. First, we introduce a density-dependent invariant region and apply the maximum principle to establish the hyperbolicity principle of the 2D self-similar Euler equations. Second, we establish a priori estimates for the shock types by differentiating the Rankine-Hugoniot conditions along the shocks, comparing the shock and acoustic speeds, and using the Oleinik-Liu entropy condition. Finally, we employ the hodograph transformation together with regularization to handle the various singularities on sonic shocks. These wave interactions serve as building blocks for more complicated 2D Riemann problems and as benchmarks for numerical algorithms for nonconvex conservation laws. We also propose several open problems.
item.dc:creator: Geng Lai, Wancheng Sheng

item.title: Rigidity for semiconvex entire solutions of Hessian quotient equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.31992v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every smooth admissible semiconvex entire solution of $\sigma_k(D^2u)/\sigma_l(D^2u)=1$ in $\mathbb R^n$, where $0\le l<k\le n$ and $k-l=1$ or $2$, is a quadratic polynomial. The proof uses a shifted Legendre transform and interior Hessian estimates for Hessian quotient equations to reduce the problem to equations of lower order. We then conclude by induction on the order of the equation.
item.dc:creator: Guohuan Qiu, Jin Yan, Xingchen Zhou, Ruixuan Zhu

item.title: Synchronized Memory-Dependent Intracellular Oscillations for a Cell-Bulk ODE-PDE Model in $\mathbb{R}^3$
item.description: arXiv:2611.32077v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a hybrid asymptotic-numerical theory for a cell-bulk ODE-PDE model in $\mathbb{R}^3$ to analyze the long-range diffusive coupling of spatially localized, dynamically active cells. In the limit of small cell radius $\varepsilon\ll 1$, we derive a novel integro-differential ODE system for the intracellular dynamics, in which the 3-D bulk diffusion field is effectively replaced by a time-memory kernel whose strength depends on the inter-cell distances. To compute long-time solutions efficiently, we implement a fast time-marching scheme for this integro-differential system that is inspired by the \emph{sum-of-exponentials} method. This scheme is applied to Sel'kov intracellular kinetics, which is a conceptual two-component model for a conditional oscillator. Our analysis reveals that, in contrast to the more strongly coupled 2-D case, each cell in $\mathbb{R}^3$ experiences only a weak $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon)$ coupling effect from the other cells in the population. Consequently, individual cells that exhibit oscillatory intracellular dynamics can only synchronize over very long time scales of order $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-1})$ when they are separated by $\mathcal{O}(1)$ distances. Moreover, cells whose kinetic parameters are $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon)$ close to their marginal stability threshold will be influenced by the weak $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon)$ cell-cell coupling from the entire population. In order to resolve the effect of these subtle interactions on collective intracellular dynamics, we develop a novel matrix perturbation theory for the linear stability of steady-state solutions of the cell-bulk model. Finally, we validate our analytical predictions of the perturbed marginal stability thresholds of steady-state solutions using the time-marching numerical scheme, illustrating various types of synchronized intracellular dynamics that can emerge over long time scales.
item.dc:creator: Merlin Pelz, Michael J. Ward

item.title: Weak--viscosity equivalence for the fractional Trudinger equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.32142v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove weak--viscosity equivalence for the fractional Trudinger equation $\partial_t(|u|^{p-2}u)+\mathcal L_{s,p}u=0$, where $1<p<\infty$ and $0<s<1$. The functions are assumed to be continuous in the equation domain and continuous in time with values in the weighted tail space. We treat both functions that are strictly positive in the equation domain, with signed exterior values, and globally nonnegative functions with interior zeros. Exterior values need not be bounded or spatially continuous. For $1<p<2$, the viscosity formulation tests the evolution variable $|u|^{p-2}u$, retaining the nonlocal interaction at zeros. The viscosity-to-weak implication follows from localized multiplicative regularization and energy estimates independent of a positive lower bound. The reverse implication uses comparison with smooth functions, justified by a relative-energy identity. A zero-slice property allows the weak identities on positive time intervals to be joined across the zero set.
item.dc:creator: Qi Xue, Chao Zhang

item.title: Relaxation dynamics of Winfree oscillators on Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.32179v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study exponential relaxation to equilibrium for Winfree-type models on Riemannian manifolds. For the sphere model with entrainment point $p$ and canonical influence, we derive convergence to equilibrium, whenever no oscillator starts at the antipode $-p$. For the corresponding canonical model on $\mathrm U(d)$, we obtain the same convergence whenever no initial matrix has the eigenvalue $-1$. Both results hold above explicit coupling thresholds depending on the initial configuration and the frequency matrices. For a broader class of unitary influence functions, the same spectral condition yields exponential convergence for sufficiently large coupling strengths. Finite-time entrance into positively invariant stable regions and contraction estimates yield exponential convergence rates and equilibrium uniqueness within those regions. A finite symmetry construction on Lie groups realizes the unitary model and a special unitary analogue as invariant Kuramoto--Lohe subsystems, yielding local relaxation results. Finally, we formulate an abstract Winfree model on Riemannian manifolds and establish local exponential relaxation in a fixed coordinate neighborhood under quantitative attraction and regularity assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Seung-Yeal Ha, Chaejoo Lee, Eunjun Lee, Jaemoon Lee, Seung-Yeon Ryoo

item.title: Observable sets for one-dimensional Schr\"odinger equations with subquadratic power potentials
item.description: arXiv:2611.32222v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study observability inequalities for the one-dimensional Schr\"odinger equation associated with the operator $H_m=-\partial_x^2+|x|^{2m}$, where $0<m\leq1$. For $0<m<1/2$, observability in some positive time, and equivalently in every positive time, is characterized by the thickness of the observation set. This extends the characterization of Chen--Liu--Liu at $m=1/2$. For $1/2<m\leq1$, we characterize observable sets in terms of the asymptotic lower density on the spatial intervals $I_{m,a}(x)=[x-a|x|^{2m-1},x+a|x|^{2m-1}]$. Observability in some positive time is equivalent to positive density at some scale, whereas observability in every positive time is equivalent to positive density at every scale. Moreover, for $1/2<m<1$, the minimal observation time is comparable to the square root of the critical density scale.
item.dc:creator: Yanchuan Wang

item.title: Magnetic vector fields with isolated singularities
item.description: arXiv:2611.32243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct unit-length, divergence-free vector fields tangent to the boundary on arbitrary smoothly bounded domains in $\mathbb R^3$. These vector fields are continuously differentiable except for a finite number of points on the boundary. Our approach identifies a form of h-principle and a close analogy with Nash's construction of smooth isometric embeddings.
item.dc:creator: L\'aszl\'o Sz\'ekelyhidi, David Ziener

item.title: $L^p$-boundedness of magnetic pseudodifferential operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.32323v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that $L^p$-boundedness for magnetic pseudodifferential operators is equivalent to $L^p$-boundedness of non-magnetic pseudodifferential operators for $p\in[1,\infty]$, regular magnetic fields and classical H\"ormander symbols $S_{\rho,\delta}^m$ with $0<\rho\leq 1$ and $0\leq\delta<1$. As a corollary we get $L^p$-boundedness for $1<p<\infty$ of magnetic pseudodifferential operators when $\rho>0,0\leq\delta\leq\rho\leq1,\delta<1$ and $m\leq-d(1-\rho)|1/2-1/p|$. Moreover, we give a bound on the operator norm in terms of the magnetic field and symbol.
item.dc:creator: Morten Nielsen, Gabriele Peluso, Mikkel Hviid Thorn

item.title: Fractional minimality of the Simons cone for $s$ close to $1$
item.description: arXiv:2611.32338v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the Simons cone in $\mathbb R^8$ minimizes the fractional perimeter $P_s$, under compact perturbations, whenever $s$ is sufficiently close to $1$.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Novaga, Emanuele Paolini

item.title: Exact Solutions and a Critical-Damping Threshold for a Nonlinear Transport-Wave Equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.32346v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Linear stability theory does not determine whether a small disturbance in a physical system decays or grows without bound when the disturbance has finite size and the damping varies in time. We address this question for the nonlinear damped transport-wave equation $u_{tt}+cu_{xt}+\gamma u_t=\lambda u(u_t+cu_x)e^{-\gamma t}$, a constant-coefficient case of a model introduced in previous work. Combining the method of characteristics with a Riccati reduction, we reduce the equation exactly to a first-order ordinary differential equation at each point and solve it explicitly. For a natural class of initial data, the solution has a critical damping rate $\gc$, given in closed form in terms of the initial data: for $\gamma<\gc$ the solution blows up in finite time, and otherwise no finite-time singularity occurs. A similar result holds for time-dependent damping and for power-law feedback. Applications to shock formation in the damped Burgers equation, gelation with decaying reactivity and frictional heating under a moving band are presented.
item.dc:creator: Sameh Gana, Salma Ben Khelifa

item.title: On the number of positive solutions of the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on compact star graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.32408v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider the number and the shape of positive solutions of the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on compact symmetric star graphs with Dirichlet condition at the exterior vertex and Kirchhoff condition at the central vertex.
item.dc:creator: Colette De Coster, Miguel Mart\'inez-Teruel

item.title: Time-uniform bounds and long-time asymptotics for a three-species drift-diffusion model for memristors
item.description: arXiv:2611.32411v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The qualitative behavior of weak solutions to the two-dimensional drift-diffusion equations for memristors, incorporating Shockley-Read-Hall-type generation-recombination terms and time-dependent boundary conditions, is investigated. The model couples the electron, hole, and oxygen-vacancy densities to the electric potential through the Poisson equation. The global existence and uniqueness of weak solutions are established. If the boundary data converge to the thermal equilibrium at an integrable rate, the densities remain uniformly-in-time bounded above and below, and the solution converges exponentially fast to thermal equilibrium. For time-independent boundary data and sufficiently small applied bias, solutions converge exponentially fast to steady states carrying nonzero fluxes.
item.dc:creator: Ansgar J\"ungel, Tuan Tung Nguyen

item.title: Notes for a seminar on vortex layer cascades
item.description: arXiv:2611.32419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: After the seminars I recently gave at New York University, the University of Chicago, Princeton University and the University of Bonn and after having been asked by some people to publish these notes, I decided to upload them to arXiv. In recent years, the method of vortex layer cascades has successfully been applied to construct finite-time singularities in multiple fluid equations (3D Euler, Boussinesq, IPM, g-SQG...). In this talk, I will motivate and describe the method and sketch how it can be applied to the 2D Boussinesq and 2D non-homogeneous Euler equations. In both systems, the growth of the vorticity is driven by an accumulated hysteresis effect triggered by the cyclic deformation of the density layers, whose dynamics is governed by an infinite chain of degenerate pendula. Our work also settles the previously open question about global existence of classical solutions of the (forced) 2D non-homogeneous Euler equations.
item.dc:creator: Andr\'es La\'in Sanclemente

item.title: Nonexistence of positive entire solutions to systems of semilinear elliptic inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2611.32435v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider the system $\Delta u \geq p(x)g(v)$, $\Delta v \geq q(x)f(|\nabla u|)$, with $u>0$ and $v>0$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, where $n\geq2$, $f,g\in C[0,\infty)$ and $p,q\in C(\mathbb{R}^n)$. If $f,g$ are non-decreasing and convex, using a comparison argument we prove a sufficient Keller-Osserman type condition for the nonexistence of entire solutions. This result is sharp for a wide class of systems. Similar results are also shown to hold for systems without gradient terms.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Devine

item.title: Shock formation in traffic flow models with Arrhenius look-ahead interactions
item.description: arXiv:2611.32449v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study finite-time shock formation in a nonlocal traffic flow model with Arrhenius look-ahead dynamics. For the constant interaction potential, we derive a time-dependent lower bound for the minimum slope and obtain a sufficient condition with logarithmic dependence on the magnitude of the minimum initial slope. For the linear interaction potential with look-ahead distance $\gamma$, we show that the condition $u'_0(x_0)>\frac{1}{\gamma}$ at a single point is sufficient for shock formation, which is independent of the minimum initial slope. Our results strictly improve the corresponding conditions of Lee and Liu \cite{r17}.
item.dc:creator: Jian Chen, Zhaonan Luo, Zhaoyang Yin

item.title: Global Weak Solutions and Non-Formation of Vacuum States for Compressible Navier--Stokes--Korteweg Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.32527v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A long-standing open problem in the mathematical theory of M-D fluid dynamics in viscous compressible flow is whether vacuum can form in finite time from initial data with density bounded away from zero. The underlying assumption in the derivation of systems of Navier--Stokes type from physical principles is that the fluid is non-dilute and can be described as a continuum. A negative answer to this problem would support the self-consistency of the continuum assumption for the Navier--Stokes-type models. This issue is particularly important when the viscosity coefficients are constant, since, from a physical standpoint, it is unclear how to meaningfully define the fluid velocity in vacuum regions, which in turn makes it difficult to interpret the associated viscous stresses. In this paper, for the barotropic compressible fluid with capillary effects, when the coefficients of viscosity and capillarity are all constants, we establish the global existence of weak solutions of the Cauchy problem for the corresponding Navier--Stokes--Korteweg equations with initial data that are large, radially symmetric, and away from the vacuum in two and three spatial dimensions. The failure of the well-known BD entropy estimate poses a substantial challenge to establishing this existence theory. Moreover, we rule out finite-time vacuum formation for the 2-D radially symmetric weak solutions constructed here. This extends, for the first time, the well-known Hoff--Smoller non-vacuum-formation theory (Commun. Math. Phys. 2001) from 1-D compressible Navier--Stokes equations with constant viscosity coefficients to 2-D radially symmetric flows with capillarity.
item.dc:creator: Yachun Li, Fangzhe Qin, Shengguo Zhu

item.title: Identifying the critical mass in a quasilinear chemotaxis model with indirect signal production
item.description: arXiv:2611.32580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The mass threshold separating boundedness and unboundedness of global solutions to a critical quasilinear parabolic-elliptic chemotaxis model with indirect signal production is identified in the radially symmetric setting in a ball. Specifically, solutions emanating from initial values with mass below a critical mass M\textsubscr{c} > 0, which is characterized in terms of a variant of the Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequality, are global and bounded. In contrast, for any M > M\textsubscr{c}, there are initial values with mass M such that the corresponding global solutions are unbounded. The proof relies on the variational structure of the system and a detailed study of the stationary states.
item.dc:creator: Philippe Lauren\c{c}ot (LAMA), Christoph Walker
