item.title: The one-velocity Baer--Nunziato system as a weak limit of solutions to a compressible two-fluid system
item.description: arXiv:2611.32601v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how a macroscopic mixture arises from two compressible fluids that share a velocity but occupy disjoint regions. We fix the initial density profiles and the common initial velocity, and let the partition between the fluids oscillate on increasingly fine scales. The fluids remain segregated as they evolve, but in the weak limit the phase indicator becomes a volume fraction that may lie strictly between zero and one. For independent adiabatic exponents $\gamma^\pm\geq9/5$, we prove that the sequence of segregated solutions converges to a global weak solution of the viscous one-velocity Baer--Nunziato system in three space dimensions. The mixture pressure is the volume-weighted average of the two phase pressures, while their difference drives the evolution of the volume fraction along the flow and contributes to dissipation in the macroscopic energy inequality.
item.dc:creator: Cosmin Burtea, Ewelina Zatorska

item.title: A sufficient criterion for ballistic behavior of forced geometric motions in random environment
item.description: arXiv:2611.32724v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a sufficient criterion for ballistic motion of interface evolutions in random environments. More precisely, we consider interfaces moving by forced mean curvature flow in dimension $d=2$ with a spatially fluctuating (possibly negative) driving force. Such models arise e.g. from the motions of dislocation lines or magnetic domain walls in a material with impurities. We show that the evolution admits an `effective minimum speed on large scales' if for a sample of the random environment in some long and thin box there is a sufficiently large probability that an interface initialized in the bottom of the box evolves to reach its top. The concept of an `effective minimum speed on large scales' was introduced and is required for the quantitative stochastic homogenization result in the companion paper ``Quantitative homogenization of forced geometric motions through random fields of obstacles''. We show that our criterion and hence the requirements for the homogenization result in the companion paper are satisfied for compactly supported obstacle shapes distributed according to a Poisson point process with sufficiently low intensity.
item.dc:creator: Julian Fischer, Jonas Ingmanns

item.title: Mixed local and fractional laplacian problems with $(\alpha,\beta)$-Neumann conditions
item.description: arXiv:2611.32779v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The existence of non-constant solutions to a mixed local-nonlocal elliptic problem with $(\alpha,\beta)$-Neumann conditions, critical exponent, and parameter $\lambda>0$ is established for any $\lambda$ large enough. Proofs exploit both mountain-pass-type arguments and appropriate boundary Sobolev inequalities patterned after those of [19].
item.dc:creator: Umberto Guarnotta, Salvatore A. Marano, Olimpio H. Miyagaki

item.title: Finite-time blowup in the inviscid GOY and Sabra models
item.description: arXiv:2611.32870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the inviscid GOY and Sabra shell models with zero boundary conditions at the lowest shells, we construct strong solutions with finitely supported initial data whose vorticity amplitudes blow up in the supremum norm in finite time, at the self-similar rate $(T-t)^{-1}$. The blowup is stable under small perturbations of the initial data in the same norm, including complex-valued ones. Guided by the work of Mailybaev, we use a travelling wave of the renormalized equations to obtain blowup in the original variables. We construct such a wave for the equations extended to all integer shells, decaying in both directions. We then show that the dynamics near this wave contract once the directions generated by time-translation and phase symmetries are removed by adjusting the symmetry parameters at each step (a modulation argument). This yields blowup solutions on the positive shells satisfying the original boundary conditions. Computer-assisted interval arithmetic is used to establish the existence of the travelling wave and the contraction estimate needed for the modulation argument.
item.dc:creator: Taehun Kim

item.title: Global regularities for the Dirichlet problem of Monge-Amp\`ere type equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.32891v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish global a priori $W^{2,p}$ and $C^{2,\alpha}$ estimates for elliptic solutions of the Dirichlet problem for cost-generated Monge-Amp\`ere type equations under the weak Ma-Trudinger-Wang condition A3w, assuming continuous and H\"older continuous right-hand sides, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Feida Jiang, Jiakun Liu, Jian Lu, Chuanlong Sun

item.title: Discretely self-similar solutions to coupled fluid systems with locally $L^2$ data
item.description: arXiv:2611.32897v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we present a systematic way to construct discretely self-similar solutions of fluid systems, including the viscous resistive magnetohydrodynamics equations, the viscoelastic Navier-Stokes equations with damping, and the Oberbeck-Boussinesq system, for locally $L^2$ initial data which are not necessarily in the uniformly local $L^2$ space. The solutions satisfy local energy inequalities, local a priori bounds depending only on the $L^2$ norm of the initial data in a fixed ball (and, for the Oberbeck--Boussinesq system, on the force), and a limiting formula for the pressure.
item.dc:creator: Chen-Chih Lai, Tai-Peng Tsai

item.title: The Kelvin--Hicks Formula from the Energy--Casimir Principle
item.description: arXiv:2611.32919v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classical Kelvin--Hicks formula expresses the propagation speed of a thin vortex ring in an incompressible ideal fluid in terms of its circulation, distance from the symmetry axis, and core radius. In this paper, we rigorously derive this formula from a variational principle based on Arnold's energy--Casimir method, without prescribing any of these geometric or physical quantities a priori. We introduce a scale-invariant variational principle involving the energy, impulse, and $L^p$ Casimir invariants. For $1 < p < \infty$, we construct orbitally stable energy-maximizing vortex rings and investigate how their geometry depends on the Casimir exponent $p$. For sufficiently large $p$, the vortex rings have cores homeomorphic to a ball and converge to Hill's spherical vortex as $p \to \infty$. In contrast, as $p\to1^+$, the energy-maximizing vortex rings concentrate onto a circular filament of radius $e^{1/3}$, uniquely selected by the variational principle. After suitable translations and rescalings, their vortex-core profiles converge to an optimizer of the logarithmic Hardy--Littlewood--Sobolev inequality. Introducing an effective core radius $\epsilon_p$ determined by the entropy of the vorticity distribution, we establish the Kelvin--Hicks formula \begin{align*} W_p = \frac{\Gamma_p}{4\pi R_p} \left(\log\frac{8R_p}{\epsilon_p}-1+o(1)\right) \quad \textrm{as}\ p\to1^+, \end{align*} where $W_p$, $\Gamma_p$, and $R_p$ denote the propagation speed, circulation, and effective ring radius, respectively. In particular, the constant correction $-1$ is obtained for nonuniform vortex-core profiles without imposing any prescribed core structure.
item.dc:creator: Ken Abe, Kwan Woo

item.title: On the phase-space geometry for Riemann solutions: rank-one structure, implicit solutions and elusive transitional shocks
item.description: arXiv:2611.32933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The effective flux function reduces a Riemann problem for a $2\times 2$ system of conservation laws to a scalar one, by lifting the wave curve. We show that the reduction rests on a rank-one property, namely that the Jacobian $\partial(u,\,v)/\partial(x,\,t)$ equals the product of the two wave strengths, up to nonzero factors, and vanishes identically for every self-similar solution. Hence the lifting needs no hypothesis for Riemann data, and for Cauchy data it survives exactly on an integral curve of an eigenvector field, where we give an implicit solution; off that curve the state path leaves it at a rate we compute. We then ask when an implicit closed-form solution exists for arbitrary data. For homogeneous quadratic fluxes these are precisely the systems linearly equivalent to two decoupled Burgers equations (the curve $a=1+b^2$ of the Schaeffer--Shearer normal form). Every such system loses strict hyperbolicity along a full line, so no model with an isolated umbilic point qualifies, among them the quadratic Corey model of three-phase flow. We close with a quadratic model in which a datum on a straight integral curve gives an exact solution with a stationary transitional shock, having one family nearly linearly degenerate at each end.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Casta\~neda

item.title: A lower bound on the Nusselt number in stochastically forced Rayleigh--B\'enard convection
item.description: arXiv:2611.32984v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a lower bound on the expected long-time averaged Nusselt number for two-dimensional Rayleigh--B\'enard convection at infinite Prandtl number, with free-slip boundaries and a suitable additive noise of amplitude $0<\sigma\leq1$ in the temperature equation. For every deterministic initial temperature, we prove that \[ \underline{Nu}-1 \geq c(\sigma^3 Ra)^{7/192}, \] provided that \[ \sigma^3 Ra \geq C(1+\log(1/\sigma))^{192/7}, \] where $c,C>0$ depend only on the domain parameter $L$. Without noise, no such bound can hold, since the conductive state is a solution with $Nu=1$ for every Rayleigh number. The proof uses the auxiliary functional method. For general Markov processes, we show that the defining inequality of an auxiliary functional need only hold after a short time average. This reduces the problem to showing that, with uniformly positive probability, the solution quickly leaves the set of states with low heat flux and low thermal dissipation. We establish this by projecting onto an unstable eigenvector of the linearization around the initial mean temperature profile, yielding a one-dimensional It\^o process with linear growth, additive noise, and nonlinear error terms.
item.dc:creator: Juraj Foldes, Jun Hyun Park

item.title: Large-time existence for the gravity water waves equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.32994v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide a new well-posedness result on the gravity water-waves equations, i.e. the free-surface, incompressible and irrotational Euler equations, in the absence of surface tension. Our main contribution is to provide the existence of solutions, in high enough but finite Sobolev regularity, on a timescale that grows like the inverse of the non-linearity parameter. Our result is also uniform in the shallow-water parameter. The main difficulty is that we allow for the presence of a large (though not emerging) bathymetry.
item.dc:creator: Th\'eo Fradin, Benjamin Melinand

item.title: On the first eigenvalue of the infinity Fractional Bilaplacian
item.description: arXiv:2611.33000v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the first eigenvalue of the infinity fractional bilaplacian under hinged and clamped exterior conditions. On bounded Lipschitz domains satisfying a uniform exterior ball condition, we establish existence of minimizers for both problems. In the hinged case, we prove uniqueness up to multiplication by a nonzero constant and identify the minimizers with the fractional torsion function. In the clamped case, an $L^p$-approximation yields a minimizer satisfying a limiting fractional PDE-system with measure data. We also prove a sharp Faber-Krahn inequality for the hinged eigenvalue, and use its explicit expression to obtain double sided estimates for the clamped eigenvalue on a ball.
item.dc:creator: Simone Carano, Alessandro Carbotti

item.title: Global Existence and Large-Time Behavior of Strong Solutions to the Two-Dimensional Full Compressible Navier-Stokes Equations with Degenerate Heat Conductivity and Large Initial Data
item.description: arXiv:2611.33110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the two-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes system with degenerate heat conductivity in three settings: the periodic domain, a general bounded simply connected domain subject to Navier-slip boundary conditions, and the whole space with non-vacuum far-field density. We assume that the shear viscosity $\mu$ is a positive constant, the bulk viscosity $\lambda(\rho)\ge0$ depends on the density, and the heat conductivity takes the form $\kappa(\theta)=\kappa_0 \theta^\alpha$ with $\kappa_0>0$. For a broad class of density-dependent bulk viscosities, we establish the global existence and large-time behavior of strong solutions for arbitrarily large initial data allowing vacuum. In particular, our results include the sublinear growth law $$ \lambda(\rho)=\frac{\rho}{(1+\rho)^\varepsilon \log\log(e^e+\rho)}, $$ where $\varepsilon>0$ is a sufficiently small constant depending only on the domain, the initial data, and the physical parameters.
item.dc:creator: Qinghao Lei, Xin Song

item.title: Low-regularity evolution and control for the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with singular bilinear interactions
item.description: arXiv:2611.33122v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the one-dimensional nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation (NLS) $i\dt \psi -\dx^2 \psi = (u(t)\cdot \mu) \psi +\kappa |\psi|^{2m}\psi,$ on the torus under the presence of singular, time-dependent bilinear external fields $(u(t)\cdot \mu)$. We prove well-posedness in $H^s(\T)$ for low regularity indices $s>\max\big\{\tfrac12-\tfrac1m,0\big\}$ ($s>0$ when $\kappa=0$), under sharp assumptions on the singular potentials, covering both the linear and nonlinear cases. We establish small-time exact controllability in $H^{\frac12+}(\T)$ for a large class of states, by combining saturation techniques with the moment method. The result extends previous bilinear exact controllability results for linear Schr\"odinger equations, which are typically obtained in large time and under high regularity assumptions. Crucial to our approach is the role of the singular time-dependent potentials, which enable the recovery of controllability properties in small time and at low regularity, overcoming obstructions present in the smooth setting.
item.dc:creator: R\'emi Buffe, Alessandro Duca, Tristan Robert

item.title: Extended group analysis and conservation laws of a class of variable coefficient generalized Kawahara equations
item.description: arXiv:2607.09482v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We review and extend the results on the group analysis of a class of generalized Kawahara equations with time-dependent coefficients. First, we provide an overview of the existing literature on Lie symmetries and Lie-invariant solutions of such equations. We then present a complete description of their transformation properties, including admissible, equivalence, and Lie symmetry transformations. For practical applications, we further extend these results by presenting a complete Lie symmetry classification without simplifying the coefficients via equivalence transformations. Lie reductions are then systematically performed, and several exact solutions are constructed. Low-order local conservation laws are exhaustively classified: every equation in this class admits conservation of mass and the squared $L^2$ norm, whereas energy-type conservation laws exist only for specific coefficient branches that align with the cases singled out by the symmetry classification. Finally, the classification results are enhanced by a study of contractions, which link cases of Lie symmetry extensions together with the associated reductions and conservation laws.
item.dc:creator: Olena Vaneeva, Alexander Zhalij, Olena Magda, Oksana Brahinets

item.title: Sharp History-Length Dependence of Mesh-Uniform Exponential Decay Rates for a Boundary-Memory Euler-Bernoulli Beam
item.description: arXiv:2611.31650v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a boundary-memory Euler--Bernoulli beam with polynomial relaxation, we quantify the loss of exponential stability as the retained history length $S$ grows. The continuous and conforming Hermite--$\mathbb P_1$ generators have zero-frequency resolvent norms bounded above and below by constant multiples of $S$. The bounds are uniform in the beam mesh and in every history mesh of step at most a fixed $h_0$. Their semigroup norms retain a plateau of duration proportional to $S$. Under positive distributed and boundary damping, matching exponential estimates hold with the optimal time scale $1+S$, uniformly in the meshes. Optimality refers to the semigroup norm on the augmented state space, which includes the history. Without distributed damping, the same time scale holds for the continuous truncated generator under a boundary condition on $\delta^{(3)}$. We also prove strong convergence of the finite-history semigroups to the full-history semigroup, uniformly on compact time intervals, under restriction and zero extension of histories. Remote-history packets give residuals of order $S^{-1}$ for the truncated generator and of order $S^{-1}+h$ after discretization, improved to $S^{-1}$ at zero frequency. Numerical tests confirm the residual orders.
item.dc:creator: Gossrin Jean-Marc Bomisso

item.title: Spectral characterizations of sub-Gaussian heat kernel bounds
item.description: arXiv:2611.31712v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Grigor'yan, Hu and Lau, in Conjecture 3.9 of [Springer Proc. Math. Stat. 88 (2014): 147--207], asked whether a Faber--Krahn inequality and matching bounds for the bottom of the Dirichlet spectrum on balls characterize sub-Gaussian heat kernel upper bounds. We give a counterexample on the Euclidean plane. Our counterexample uses a planar diffusion associated with a Dirichlet form from the work of Li and Sun in [Ann. Appl. Probab. 34 (2024), 4193--4236]. The bottom of the Dirichlet spectrum on every ball of radius $r$ is comparable to $r^{-2}$ meanwhile for balls centered on the $x_1$-axis, the mean exit time starting at the center is comparable to $r^3$ as $r\downarrow0$. This also shows that the exit-time hypotheses used to characterize heat kernel upper bounds in [Stochastic Process. Appl. 189 (2025): 104707] and [Math. Nachr. 299 (2026): 2566--2589] cannot be omitted. We then give a novel spectral characterization of heat kernel upper bounds in terms of the first Dirichlet eigenpair of balls. In particular, on an unbounded proper geodesic Dirichlet space with volume doubling, reverse volume doubling and a scale-$r^\beta$ Poincar\'e inequality, the heat kernel upper estimate is equivalent to $\lambda(B(x,r))\asymp r^{-\beta}$ and a uniform comparison between the supremum of a nonnegative first eigenfunction and its value at $x$. Under elliptic Harnack inequality, we also prove that the mean exit-time scale on balls is equivalent to the scale on the bottom of the spectrum on balls. This proves Conjecture~4.15 of Grigor'yan, Hu and Lau. The Euclidean planar example given above also disproves the eigenvalue version of their Conjecture~4.16 on a characterization of the parabolic harnack inequality. We end by showing that our spectral conditions gives the correct characterization.
item.dc:creator: Phanuel Mariano, Jing Wang

item.title: A mixed-primal FEM for Poisson-Fermi interfacial problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.31722v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper presents a mixed-primal FEM for a linearised Poisson--Fermi interface problem arising from the Bazant--Storey--Kornyshev theory, which describes electrostatic interactions in ionic solutions. It leads to a transmission problem coupling a fourth-order equation in the solvent region with a second-order equation in the solute region. To precisely compute the electrostatic stress and the interactive force in the electrolyte, we reformulate the fourth-order problem as a mixed system by introducing the gradient of the electrostatic potential, the divergence of its gradient, and the gradient of its divergence as additional independent variables. The second-order problem is studied in its primal form as this approach eliminates the requirement for Lagrange multipliers to enforce the transmission conditions. The resulting formulation is discretised using Raviart--Thomas finite elements for the vector variables and piecewise polynomial finite elements for the scalar variables. Well-posedness of the mixed-primal formulation and optimal a priori error estimates for the field variables as well as for the postprocessed Maxwell tensor are established under suitable regularity assumptions, in parameter-weighted norms in which the inf-sup constant is independent of the correlation length and of the permittivity ratio. The constants in the error estimates are independent of both parameters as well, up to a loss of at most half an order when the mesh does not resolve the length scale (square root of the relative permittivity); the Sobolev norms of the solution may still depend on the parameters through boundary layers. The postprocessed Maxwell stress converges with optimal order on quasi-uniform meshes, except for the lowest-order scheme in 3D. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical convergence rates and demonstrate the properties of the proposed method for problems in 2D and 3D.
item.dc:creator: Siyad Rahman Mandottil, Neela Nataraj, Ricardo Ruiz-Baier

item.title: Upwind finite element approximation of the gradient blow-up time for a viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.31859v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We analyze an upwind finite element method with piecewise linear elements for a viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation with a superquadratic gradient source term, subject to homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. On polytopal inner approximations of smooth bounded domains in dimensions $N=1,2,3$, we prove maximum-norm convergence of the numerical solution to the exact solution before gradient blow-up and convergence of gradient-threshold times to the blow-up time under explicit mesh and regularity assumptions. We also verify the regularity assumption and finite-time gradient blow-up for an example on the disk, to which the main theorem therefore applies. Numerical experiments illustrate this gradient blow-up.
item.dc:creator: Yohei Fujishima, Takahiro Yamada

item.title: The polygonal Steklov--Weinstock inequality
item.description: arXiv:2611.32028v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that for every integer $N \ge 3$, the regular $N$-gon uniquely maximizes the scale-invariant first positive Steklov eigenvalue $L(P)\sigma_1(P)$ among all simple planar polygons $P$ of positive area with at most $N$ sides, up to similarity (and up to congruence at prescribed perimeter). Our proof combines two complementary realizations of the Rayleigh--Ritz variational principle. For convex competitors, we transplant a first Steklov eigenfunction of the regular reference polygon: for triangles, affine transplantation aligned with a longest side yields both the sharp inequality and a two-sided linear stability bound in terms of the maximal side-length deviation; for convex $N$-gons with $N \ge 4$, a piecewise harmonic fan transplantation across radial sectors matches traces along the internal seams. In the quadrilateral case, centering the fan at the vertex average pairs opposite sides and controls the displacement of the diagonal midpoints, whereas for $N=5$ the spectral deficit dominates both the area deficit and the squared vertex and Hausdorff distances to the regular pentagon. Nonconvex competitors are treated by stratifying them according to their number $p \le N-1$ of strictly convex corners: boundary moment inequalities handle $p=3$, while conformal disk tests localized on the gaps between positive turning prevertices rule out $p \ge 4$ via comparison with the regular $(p+1)$-gon. Finite parameter ranges are certified using exact rational arithmetic and outward-rounded integer interval enclosures. In addition, we establish the sharp fourth-order asymptotic expansion of the spectral deficit at a prescribed positive-corner count, together with a quantitative local and global stability theorem for polygons with a large number of sides.
item.dc:creator: Zhuo Cheng, Yian Zhang

item.title: Group classification of a class of systems of nonlinear diffusion equations. I
item.description: arXiv:2611.32136v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the Lie symmetries of a class of systems of (1 + 1)-dimensional nonlinear diffusion equations. The equivalence algebra and the kernel of the maximal Lie invariance algebras of this class are found. We prove that there exist exactly nine inequivalent subclasses of this class for which the corresponding diffusion systems admit Lie symmetry extensions. We also carry out the exhaustive group classification of the systems of nonlinear diffusion equations from the first subclass.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Voloshyn, O., Serov, M. & Vaneeva, O. Group Classification of a Class of Systems of Nonlinear Diffusion Equations. I. Ukr Math J 78, 40 (2026)
item.dc:creator: Oleksandr A. Voloshyn, Mykola I. Serov, Olena O. Vaneeva

item.title: Rotationally symmetric fractional minimal surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.32252v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we provide a non-trivial example of an $s$-minimal surface that is invariant under rotations. More precisely, we study alternating radial sets whose boundaries are finite or locally finite unions of concentric spheres and prove that, fixing the outer radius to $r=1$, there exists a radial configuration for which the fractional mean curvature $H_s$ vanishes at every free interface. We then show that rescaling radial maximizers by their innermost radius and passing to the limit yields a properly embedded, rotationally symmetric, locally finite hypersurface satisfying $H_s=0$ at every point of the boundary.
item.dc:creator: Chiara Gambicchia, Matteo Novaga, Matteo Talluri

item.title: Equivariant harmonic maps from $\mathbb{S}^3$ to $\mathbb{S}^2$: on a counterexample to a conjecture of J. Eells
item.description: arXiv:2611.32603v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The present paper builds on a remarkable AI-generated counterexample to a long-standing conjecture of James Eells. We present the rigorous construction of a smooth harmonic map $f:\mathbb{S}^3\to \mathbb{S}^2$ between the round spheres which does not factor through a Hopf fibration, and improve some arguments to get that the Hopf invariant of $f$ is either $0$ or $\pm 6$. The construction is based on a min-max scheme in a $5$-equivariant class of maps $f$ with an additional dihedral symmetry. By passing to a suitable associated sphere bundle over $\mathbb{S}^2$, the problem is reduced to a variational problem for sections, where the imposed symmetries guarantee the mountain pass structure and the non-constancy of the desired limit harmonic map.
item.dc:creator: Qi Guo, Marco Magliaro, Luciano Mari, Andreas Savas-Halilaj

item.title: Twisted Poincar\'e series at zero on surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.32648v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $(\Sigma,g)$ be a closed, connected, oriented, Riemannian Anosov surface. We show that there exists an open subset $\mathcal V_g$ of the space of finite-dimensional irreducible representations of the fundamental group of $\Sigma$, whose complement has complex codimension at least one, such that the following holds: for all $x,y\in \Sigma$, $\rho \in \mathcal{V}_g$, the meromorphic extension of the twisted Poincar\'e series $s \mapsto \eta_{g,\rho,x,y}(s)$ vanishes at $s=0$. We also give examples of non-trivial representations whose Poincar\'e series does not vanish at zero. In addition, we describe the structure of twisted resonant states at zero for these examples and show that they admit non-trivial Jordan blocks.
item.dc:creator: Tristan Humbert, Thibault Lefeuvre, Sebasti\'an Mu\~noz-Thon, Zhongkai Tao

item.title: Convergence of Implicit Particle Methods for Wasserstein Gradient Flows
item.description: arXiv:2611.32784v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we establish the convergence of implicit particle methods for Wasserstein gradient flows as the number of particles tends to infinity, with the time step held fixed. The schemes combine the Jordan--Kinderlehrer--Otto (JKO) variational time discretization with particle approximations of the evolving probability measure. The main challenge lies in approximating the internal energy, which depends nonlinearly on the probability density and cannot, in general, be evaluated directly on empirical measures. We consider three approaches: a one-dimensional density reconstruction based on the spacings between ordered particles; a blob method using kernel-based density reconstruction; and a transport-map formulation in which the density is recovered from the pushforward relation through the change-of-variables formula. The latter two approaches apply in arbitrary spatial dimensions without requiring the spatial domain to be compact. For the blob method, we also establish simultaneous convergence as the particle number tends to infinity and the regularization parameter vanishes, under the scaling $N\varepsilon_N^d\to\infty$. Our analysis combines $\Gamma$-convergence and compactness arguments to establish convergence of the discrete variational problems and their minimizers. These results complement classical dynamical mean-field theory by providing a variational particle-to-continuum limit for implicit JKO schemes involving nonlinear internal energies.
item.dc:creator: Yunhong Deng, Wilfrid Gangbo, Li Wang

item.title: Mirror flow for semimartingale optimal transport
item.description: arXiv:2611.32785v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Semimartingale optimal transport arises in a wide range of applications, including mathematical finance and flow-based generative models. A recurring computational challenge is that the dual energy functional is often poorly conditioned with respect to the dual potential, leading to slow convergence of gradient descent algorithms. To address this issue, we investigate a mirror flow approach that effectively preconditions the dual energy functional. We establish the geometric convergence of the mirror descent sequence. To obtain a practical numerical algorithm, we introduce a feasible discrete-time scheme based on first-order linearization. We prove that the scheme is well-defined and establish a uniform-in-time error bound for the accumulated linearization error, under a suitable smallness condition on the initial error. Finally, we apply the proposed mirror flow scheme to the specific-entropic martingale optimal transport (SEMOT) problem \cite{BuetGolfouseEtAl2026SEMOT} and observe a substantial improvement in computational efficiency.
item.dc:creator: Francois Buet-Golfouse, Ana\"is Despr\'es, Anna Kazeykina, Zhenjie Ren

item.title: Ancient solutions of mean curvature flow in a slab
item.description: arXiv:2611.32887v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study complete ancient solutions of the mean curvature flow in arbitrary codimension contained in slabs in Euclidean space. Under a natural principal-angle condition, we prove that a translating soliton contained in a slab of width less than $\pi$ cannot be bounded from below in the translating direction, and characterize the grim reaper cylinder in form of a rigidity result at the critical width $\pi$. We derive corresponding results for ancient solutions confined in slabs.
item.dc:creator: Niels Martin M{\o}ller, Andreas Savas-Halilaj, Knut Smoczyk

item.title: Sharp double logarithmic Brezis-Gallou\"et-Wainger inequalities in dimension four
item.description: arXiv:1301.2353v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The space $H^2(\mathbb{R}^4)$ is not contained in $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^4)$. For functions in $H^2_0$ of the unit ball of $\mathbb{R}^4$ that are also H\"older continuous of order $\alpha$, the supremum norm can nevertheless be controlled by the $L^2$ norm of the Laplacian, at the cost of a logarithm of the H\"older seminorm. We determine the optimal leading constant in this estimate. With a double logarithmic correction, the optimal constant is $1/(8\pi^2\alpha)$. With a single logarithm, the estimate holds for every larger constant and fails for $1/(8\pi^2\alpha)$ itself. No symmetry assumption is made. The proof reduces the question to a biharmonic obstacle problem with an obstacle of H\"older type. Its minimizer is radial and explicit, and the sharp constant is determined by the asymptotic behaviour of the free boundary radius. We also derive versions of these inequalities on balls and on the whole space. The results are second-order analogues in dimension four of the two-dimensional inequalities of Ibrahim, Majdoub and Masmoudi.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Majdoub, Tarek Saanouni

item.title: The Green function for waves on the $2$-regular Bethe lattice
item.description: arXiv:1711.01363v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute an explicit analytic expression for the Green function of the wave operator on the $2$-regular lattice called the ``Bethe lattice'', equipped with its standard metric. In particular, we exhibit a phenomenon of abnormal speed of propagation for waves: the effective speed of propagation of energy for large time is $c_*=2\sqrt2/3<1$, and there is a true propagation at any speed $c<c_*$. We also show that the propagator at integer times has two $\ell^2$ eigenvectors, with eigenvalues $\pm1$. They are standing waves whose amplitude is halved at each generation, and they keep one third of the energy of an initial Dirac mass trapped near the source for all times.
item.dc:creator: Ka\"is Ammari, Gilles Lebeau

item.title: Classification of solutions to the energy-critical complex Ginzburg-Landau equation and application to NLS
item.description: arXiv:2402.18347v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For the energy-critical complex Ginzburg--Landau equation, we establish a dichotomy between global existence and finite-time blow-up below the ground-state energy. At the threshold energy, we classify solutions and describe their dynamics in terms of the \(\dot H^1\) norm of the initial data relative to that of the ground state. These results and their application to energy-critical focusing nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations extend our previous work [J. Math. Pures Appl., 2026] to all dimensions \(d\ge3\) and to the ground-state energy threshold. Furthermore, we strengthen the weak--strong uniqueness result for the focusing NLS by removing the additional smallness assumption imposed in our previous work.
item.dc:creator: Xing Cheng, Chang-Yu Guo, Yunrui Zheng

item.title: Well-Posedness of the Hodge Wave Equation on a Compact Manifold
item.description: arXiv:2502.01514v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we study the Hodge wave equation on a compact orientable manifold. We present the necessary differential geometry language to treat Sobolev spaces of differential forms and use these tools to identify a boundary triplet for the problem. We use this boundary triplet to determine a class of boundary conditions for which the problem is well-posed.
item.dc:creator: Filippo Testa

item.title: Existence and uniqueness of solutions of degenerate elliptic equations with lower order terms
item.description: arXiv:2507.03818v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the existence and uniqueness of solutions to a Dirichlet problem \[ \begin{cases} Lu = f + v^{-1}\text{Div}(v{\bf e} h), & x \in \Omega; u = 0, & x \in \partial \Omega, \end{cases}\] where $L$ is a degenerate, linear, second order elliptic operator with lower order terms. We assume very weak hypotheses, in terms of the coefficients of the equation, and we also assume the existence of degenerate Sobolev and Poincar\'e inequalities. One notable feature of our result is that we show that we can assume significantly weaker versions of the Sobolev inequality if we in turn assume stronger integrability conditions on the coefficients. Our theorems generalize a number of results in the literature on degenerate elliptic equations.
item.dc:creator: Seyma Cetin, David Cruz-Uribe, Feyza Elif Dal, Scott Rodney, Yusuf Zeren

item.title: Quantitative Borg-Levinson theorem for the magnetic Sch\"odinger operator with unbounded electrical potential
item.description: arXiv:2601.15847v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The first author established in [8] a quantitative Borg-Levinson theorem for the Schr\"odinger operator with unbounded potential. In the present work, we extend the results in [8] to the magnetic Schr\"odinger operator. We discuss both the isotropic and anisotropic cases. We establish H\"older stability inequalities of determining the electrical potential or magnetic field from the corresponding boundary spectral data.
item.dc:creator: Mourad Choulli, Hiroshi Takase

item.title: Transmission and Reflection coefficients for Schr\"odinger Operators with Truncated Periodic Potentials that support defect states
item.description: arXiv:2601.22544v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider scattering waves through truncated periodic potentials with perturbations that support localized gap eigenstates. In a small complex neighborhood around an assumed positive bound state of the model operator, we prove the existence of a distinct zero reflection state, or transmission resonance. We compare its location to a previously found scattering resonance and use the properties of solutions near these interesting points to analyze the behavior of transmission and reflection coefficients of scattering solutions near the assumed bound state. By example, we also discuss the truncated simple harmonic oscillator and compare the analysis to the crystalline case.
item.dc:creator: Joseph C. Stellman, Jeremy L. Marzuola

item.title: Direct Scattering of the Focusing Nonlinear Schr\"odinger Equation with Step-like Oscillatory Initial Data
item.description: arXiv:2603.02855v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this manuscript we set up the direct and inverse scattering problems for step-like traveling wave solutions of the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation. Specifically, we consider the initial data $u_0(x)=u_e^\ell(x)$ for $x<0$ and $u_0(x)=u_e^r(x)$ for $x>0$, where $u_e^\ell(x)$ and $u_e^r(x)$ are elliptic traveling wave solutions of NLS. More generally, we consider initial data satisfying $u_0(x)\to u_e^\ell(x)$ as $x\to-\infty$ and $u_0(x)\to u_e^r(x)$ as $x\to+\infty$. Under the assumption that $u_0-u_e^\ell \in L^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^-)$ and $u_0-u_e^r \in L^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^+)$, we formulate the direct scattering problem and establish analytic properties of the scattering data. We then formulate the inverse problem as a Riemann--Hilbert problem and prove its solvability, thus proving the existence of the nonlinear Schr\"odinger solution with the above step-like initial data. Finally, we observe that our Riemann--Hilbert formulation is a special case of the one arising for full soliton-gas initial data.
item.dc:creator: Tamara Grava, Robert Jenkins, Xiaofan Zhang, Zechuan Zhang

item.title: Local solutions to hyperbolic systems with fractional dissipation
item.description: arXiv:2606.26887v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the local Cauchy problem for a class of hyperbolic quasilinear evolution systems with fractional dissipation and commutators of the fractional Laplacian $(-\Delta)^{\alpha}$ with arbitrary $\alpha\in(0,1)$ in the framework of Sobolev spaces. The analysis is motivated by the compressible Euler alignment system with singular communication weights. We show that the contribution of the commutators to the energy is absorbed by the dissipation. Our approach does not rely on the cancellation condition previously used to recover the coercivity of the highest order nonlocal terms. We further show that the commutator term induces a loss of regularity in the stability estimates, preventing the standard contraction argument from being applied. Therefore, we instead establish the relative compactness of the solution operator and apply Schauder's fixed point theorem to provide local existence for large initial data. The resulting theory identifies the obstacles to deduce local uniqueness in the presence of commutators.
item.dc:creator: Felipe Angeles

item.title: Edge State Propagation Near Multiple and Singular Interfaces
item.description: arXiv:2607.24069v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the semiclassical propagation of edge-states for a two-dimensional Dirac operator with a spatially varying mass. The zero set of the mass models the interface between topological phases and is allowed either to consist of two disjoint smooth curves or to possess an isolated singular point. For disjoint interfaces, we prove that a wave packet initially localized on one component remains confined near this interface over long semiclassical time scales and we quantify the influence of the distance between the two components on the accuracy of the approximation. For singular interfaces, we determine the regime in which the wave-packet approximation remains valid as the packet approaches the singularity and identify the scaling at which our estimates lose their uniformity.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Frantz (LAREMA, UA), {\'E}ric Vacelet (LAREMA, UA)

item.title: Global mild solutions and the semiclassical limit for the Fermi--Dirac BGK model
item.description: arXiv:2609.08142v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove global existence of mild solutions to the spatially inhomogeneous Fermi--Dirac BGK equation for arbitrary-size Pauli-admissible initial data with finite mass and kinetic energy, allowing both vacuum and locally saturated zero-temperature states. The construction relies on a moment-compatible regularization of the local equilibrium that preserves the Pauli bound and uniform moment control while remaining consistent up to the saturation boundary. The solutions satisfy mass, momentum, and energy conservation and, under an additional finite spatial second-moment assumption, an entropy-gap H-theorem on the full Pauli interval. Under uniform moment and entropy bounds, we further prove that, after extraction of a subsequence, quantum mild solutions converge strongly in phase space, uniformly on bounded time intervals, to a mild solution of the classical BGK equation.
item.dc:creator: Young-Pil Choi, Byung-Hoon Hwang, Sihyun Song

item.title: Velocity Averaging for the Wigner Equation with Electromagnetic Fields
item.description: arXiv:2609.21885v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We discuss the application of $L^2$-based velocity averaging to the Wigner kinetic equation governing the quantum evolution of the Wigner transform of a density operator of a particle subjected to an external electromagnetic field. This extends the $L^2$-based averaging lemma from [F. Golse, J. M\"oller: Commun. Math. Sci. (2026)] to electromagnetic fields. We make use of the magnetic or gauge-invariant Wigner transform due to Stratonovich [Sov. Phys. Dokl., 1:414-418, 1956] which differs from the usual definition by a phase factor involving the circulation of the magnetic vector potential along a line segment. The magnetic Wigner transform obeys the Wigner equation in the generalized phase space variables $(x,v=\xi-A(t,x))$, which is a more natural setting for the application of velocity averaging. Since the magnetic Wigner equation contains a first order derivative in the spatial variable, we obtain compactness in $L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ but no gain in regularity.
item.dc:creator: Fran\c{c}ois Golse, Jakob M\"oller

item.title: A Pogorelov-type estimate for the real twisted Monge-Amp\`ere equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.00543v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a Pogorelov type interior $C^2$ estimate for the real twisted Monge-Ampere equation without assuming uniform ellipticity. This equation is fully nonlinear and elliptic, but is neither concave nor a function of the eigenvalues of the Hessian, so the standard techniques for interior second-derivative estimates do not directly apply. Building on the partial Legendre transform formulation of Streets and Warren, we derive a differential identity for the associated positive-definite matrix $W(D^2u)$ and use some linear algebra to control the third-order terms arising in the maximum principle argument. As an application, we prove a Liouville theorem for entire split convex solutions with quadratic growth, extending the rigidity theorem of Streets and Warren by replacing their uniform ellipticity hypothesis with suitable quadratic growth assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Jordan

item.title: Isolated yet highly unstable 2D Euler equilibria
item.description: arXiv:2611.09444v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct steady solutions of the two-dimensional Euler equations on smooth annular domains that are isolated, modulo scaling, in the $L^\infty$ vorticity topology. They are highly unstable: any Yudovich trajectory remaining sufficiently close to such an equilibrium on an open time interval is a stationary multiple of it, they admit wandering neighborhoods of initial data for all non-zero time and, moreover, at fixed energy, enstrophy and circulations, distinct nearby trajectories cannot return even weakly to the equilibrium. Further, on any non-circular annular domain, we show that this kind of isolated, highly unstable equilibria occurs arbitrarily close in the Yudovich norm to smooth equilibria which are themselves non-isolated.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Enciso, Antonio J. Fern\'andez, Marc Nualart

item.title: Discrete unique continuation for Schr\"odinger equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.17073v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study discrete unique continuation for one-dimensional Schr\"odinger equations. We prove that if a solution vanishes at the points $\pm n^{\alpha}$ at time $0$ and at the points $\pm n^{\beta}$ at time $1$, it must vanish identically in two main cases: the case of a Schr\"odinger equation with a real potential that is uniformly of Gevrey class $\sigma\ge 0$ in space, provided that $\max\{1,\sigma\}\big(\alpha/(1-\alpha)+\beta/(1-\beta)\big)<1$, and in the case of the cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation, provided that $\alpha/(1-\alpha)+\beta/(1-\beta)<1$. Unlike previous results for logarithmically spaced zeros, our methods do not rely on complex analysis. We first show that, whenever $\alpha+\beta<1$, the zeros force the solution to lie in the Schwartz class at all times. We then convert the zeros into gaussian decay at the two times, by combining energy estimates for iterations of the vector field $\Gamma=x+2it\partial_x$ with techniques from Fourier uniqueness problems, and conclude with the Morgan-type uncertainty principle of Escauriaza, Kenig, Ponce and Vega.
item.dc:creator: Torunn S. Jensen, Didier Pilod, Jo\~ao P. G. Ramos

item.title: Well-posedness and finite-time breakdown for Euler-alignment systems with diffusive chemotaxis
item.description: arXiv:2611.27940v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate a recent class of pressureless Euler systems arising in biological contexts, in which the velocity evolution is driven, besides the nonlocal alignment interaction, by the gradient of a concentration self-produced by the population. We first establish local existence and uniqueness of strong solutions, in a class requiring no spatial derivative of the initial population density, together with a continuation criterion. We then derive sufficient conditions on the initial data for finite-time breakdown in the multidimensional setting, with an explicit upper bound for the maximal time of existence. Numerical simulations complement the analysis and illustrate the transition between regular and singular regimes, and the role of the chemotactic strength in the onset of blow-up.
item.dc:creator: Marta Menci, Marco Papi

item.title: Strict hot spots and absence of interior critical points on simply connected planar H\"older domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.29324v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Every nonzero real eigenfunction for the first positive Neumann eigenvalue on a bounded simply connected planar H\"older domain has no interior critical point. The H\"older condition is quasihyperbolic; equivalently, a Riemann map has derivative in $L^{2p}$ for some $p>1$. This includes Lipschitz domains and polygons with reentrant corners. Multiple eigenvalues and non-Jordan boundaries are allowed. The proof uses boundary primitives, a uniform multiplier estimate, and approximation of the whole limiting eigenspace. When this eigenspace is two-dimensional, every real basis gives global coordinates onto a domain star-shaped about the origin. A stream function proves injectivity and yields a Poisson formula for the boundary angular derivative. The conformal boundary map has a Lipschitz inverse and a rectifiable Jordan image; its boundary angle is a circle diffeomorphism with nonvanishing H\"older-continuous derivative. The image can be nonconvex even when the source is smooth and strictly convex.
item.dc:creator: Yutian Li

item.title: A posteriori error estimates for Runge-Kutta discontinuous Galerkin approximations of nonlinear convection-diffusion systems
item.description: arXiv:2510.09449v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This work provides reliable a posteriori error estimates for Runge-Kutta discontinuous Galerkin approximations of nonlinear convection-diffusion systems. The classes of systems we study are quite general, with a focus on convection-dominated problems and systems with partial diffusion. Our a posteriori error bounds are valid for a family of discontinuous Galerkin spatial discretizations and various temporal discretizations that include explicit and implicit-explicit time-stepping schemes, popular tools for practical simulations of this class of problem. We prove that our estimators provide reliable upper bounds for the error of the numerical method and present numerical evidence showing that, in the convection-dominated regime, the residual quantities converge at the same rates as the discretization errors. Since one of our main interests is the convection dominant case, we also track the dependence of the estimator on the viscosity coefficient.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Dedner, Jan Giesselmann, Kiwoong Kwon, Tristan Pryer

item.title: Quantitative homogenization for the critical long-range random conductance model
item.description: arXiv:2604.21143v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the long-range random conductance model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ at the critical exponent: the jump rate between sites $x$ and $y$ is $\mathbf{a}(\{x,y\}) |x-y|^{-(d+2)}$, where the conductances $\mathbf{a}(\{x,y\})$ are independent, uniformly elliptic and have a common mean. Below the critical exponent $(d+2)$ the walk converges to a stable process; above it, to Brownian motion with diffusive $\sqrt{t}$ scaling. At criticality the second moment of the jump kernel diverges logarithmically. We establish quantitative homogenization of the associated heat equation at the rate $1/\sqrt{|\ln \varepsilon|}$. As a consequence, we deduce annealed convergence of the random walk to Brownian motion under the anomalous $\sqrt{t \log t}$ scaling. Unlike in standard homogenization, the effective diffusivity is determined by the mean conductance alone, with no corrector contribution at leading order.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Bou-Rabee, Paul Dario

item.title: Endowing phase-field fracture models with custom strength criteria
item.description: arXiv:2606.06169v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: By now, several approaches have been proposed to endow phase-field fracture models with the ability to describe crack nucleation under multiaxial stress states. These include techniques for splitting the free energy, direct modifications of the phase-field driving or resisting forces, and the introduction of additional internal variables, such as plastic strains or other nonlinear strains. In this paper, we propose a fundamentally different strategy for incorporating arbitrary elastic domains into phase-field fracture models, formulated within the energetic framework of generalized standard materials. The proposed approach relies on letting the dissipation potential depend on the current state of the material. In this way, the elastic degradation and the strength criterion remain two distinct and independently controllable aspects of the material response, while the governing equations directly descend from a local stability condition and energy balance. Simple yet representative models are presented and thoroughly discussed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology. The resulting evolution of the elastic domain is investigated in both strain and stress spaces under proportional and non-proportional loading paths, with the latter highlighting the path dependence of the dissipated work. Moreover, numerical simulations demonstrate a range of crack nucleation processes under multiaxial loading conditions for various analytical strength surfaces. The present work paves the way for future developments and applications in several directions, including crack propagation studies and dedicated numerical solution strategies.
item.dc:creator: Roberto Alessi, Matteo Brunetti, Roshan Udaram Patil, Jacinto Ulloa

item.title: Large-time behavior and accuracy of the Mean-Field Ensemble Kalman Filter in the Linear Detectable Setting
item.description: arXiv:2606.07729v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF), originally developed in the geophysical sciences, is now widely used for state and parameter estimation problems in various domains of application, and in particular in high dimensional settings. It may be viewed as a robust, cheap-to-implement,alternative to the optimal, Bayesian, filter. However, despite its empirical successes, theoretical understanding of its properties, in relation to the optimal filter, is in its infancy. We contribute novel theoretical understanding, studying the behavior of the EnKF in the infinite particle number setting; this is known as the mean-field ensemble Kalman filter (MFEnKF). In the linear setting with Gaussian noise and Gaussian initial data the MFEnKF coincides with the optimal filter, which is characterized by the Kalman filter. Our focus in this paper will be the linear setting with Gaussian noise, but with non-Gaussian initial data. Under the assumptions of nondegeneracy of the signal noise and detectability of the signal-observation pair we make three specific contributions, studying both discrete and continuous formulations of the methodology. First, in discrete time, we derive the MFEnKF via a variational approximation of the Bayes update using a covariance-weighted optimal transport metric. Secondly, we use this metric to show that the MFEnKF is a strict contraction towards the subspace of Gaussian measures, giving explicit geometric rates in terms of the covariances, in both discrete and continuous time. Finally, in the continuous-time setting, we deduce a stable form of almost sure accuracy of the MFEnKF: given any pair of initial laws (satisfying mild conditions) for the MFEnKF and the optimal filter, the 2-Wasserstein distance between their distributions decays exponentially, for almost every observation path.
item.dc:creator: Franca Hoffmann, Sangmin Park, Andrew M. Stuart

item.title: A Unified Heat-Ball Framework for Fokker--Planck Equations: Mean-Value Identities, Exact Sampling, and Error Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2606.27954v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Diffusion-based generative models with nonlinear or learned forward drifts raise questions that stay hidden for Gaussian forward processes: how the divergence-free and gradient parts of the drift shape the evolving density, whether sampling can draw on local rather than global information, and how to treat low-density regions, where $u$ carries a weak signal while $\log u$ diverges and the entropy density $u\log u$ falls between the two. These questions motivate the present study of local representations for Fokker--Planck equations with general, possibly nonlinear and time-dependent drift. We derive inhomogeneous heat-ball identities for the density $u$, the log-density $\log u$, the entropy density $u\log u$, and the score $\nabla\log u$, keeping the source terms generated by the drift; their unscaled residuals recover the corresponding differential residuals at leading order in the squared heat-ball radius. The weights appearing in the identities, the source integrals, and the integration-by-parts formulas all belong to a single Beta--Gamma family of measures on the heat ball, which gives exact rejection-free sampling, product quadrature, and unbiased Monte Carlo estimators with variance and cost bounds that are explicit in the dimension and the radius. Experiments with Gaussian-mixture and nonlinear-drift references, in dimensions up to $1024$ where applicable, confirm the sampling laws, the identities, and the residual behavior. In particular, log-density and score evaluations remain accurate where direct density estimation breaks down, and the heat-ball residuals provide local consistency tests for learned score models. A study of gauge-based heat-ball walks illustrates a recursive use of the density identity.
item.dc:creator: Jiayao Bai, Yi Du, Rongxing Lai, Yifei Jia

item.title: An Orlicz variational formula for David-type Beltrami equations
item.description: arXiv:2608.05618v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a Banach-space variational theory for degenerate Beltrami equations of David type. For coefficients supported in a bounded domain $\mathcal{U}\subset\mathbb{C}$, the pointwise change of variables $\nu=2\mu/(1-|\mu|^2)$ identifies the David coefficients with the exponential Orlicz space $L^\Phi_{\mathcal{U}}(\mathbb{C})$ for $\Phi(s)=e^s-s-1$. On the open subset of parameters with a sufficiently large exponential moment, the principal solution map is locally real $C^{1,1}$ into $W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{C})$, with Fr\'echet derivative solving the linearized Beltrami equation. On the Orlicz heart $E^\Phi_{\mathcal{U}}(\mathbb{C})$ it is real $C^\infty$, yet fails to be real analytic at zero: along any direction $h$, its Taylor series at zero has radius of convergence $1/\|h\|_\infty$ in $W^{1,2}(B)$ for every disk $B\supset\overline{\mathcal{U}}$. Finally, for $\mathcal{U}=\mathbb{D}$, the exterior Schwarzian map from $E^\Phi_{\mathbb{D}}(\mathbb{C})$ to the little logarithmic Bers space is continuous, but fails to be Fr\'echet differentiable at zero; moreover, its zero fiber is not a $C^1$ embedded Banach submanifold near zero, obstructing any local $C^1$ split submersion structure on the resulting quotient.
item.dc:creator: Ryo Matsuda

item.title: Cutoff beyond non-negative curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.26019v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study how a relaxed gradient estimate is enough to prove cutoff for several new families of Markov processes, within the varentropy framework of [Sal25]. In particular, we show how certain regularization estimates from hypocoercivity theory allow one to prove cutoff for kinetic dynamics. Moreover, we prove cutoff for some families of diffusions with non-convex potentials and for mean-field dynamics, as well as for biased random walks on the symmetric group, giving a simple proof of a far-reaching extension of a result of [NY24].
item.dc:creator: Max Fathi, Arnaud Guillin, Cyril Labb\'e, Justin Salez

item.title: Two-scale band geometry and ballistic transport for limit-periodic Schr\"odinger operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.01303v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove strong ballistic transport for one-dimensional Schr\"odinger operators with bounded limit-periodic potentials. If the nested periodic approximants satisfy $\|V-V_n\|_\infty=o(p_{n+1}^{-2}e^{-\eta p_n})$, with $\eta>7\sqrt{2R}$ and $\|V\|_\infty\le R$, then the rescaled Heisenberg position has a nonzero strong limit on a weighted $H^2$ class containing the Schwartz space. In contrast to earlier continuum results requiring exponential accuracy in $p_{n+1}$, the exponential weight here involves only $p_n$; the ratios $p_{n+1}/p_n$ may be unbounded. Folding identifies each ordered large-cell band, away from symmetry momenta, with a fixed translated small-cell band. This confines near-collisions of all bands to a common neighborhood controlled at the smaller period. A period-uniform quadratic-form estimate, ordered-gap summation, and a graph-norm comparison linear in the potential error then give the limiting velocity. Moments of orders $0<r\le4$ have two-sided ballistic growth as a corollary. An explicit example separates the two approximation conditions.
item.dc:creator: Moises Gomez Solis

item.title: Quadrature-Induced Local Minima in Structure-Preserving Lotka-Volterra Control
item.description: arXiv:2611.20131v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study how the choice of harvest quadrature affects optimal control in a positivity-preserving Lotka--Volterra scheme. With harvesting alone, counting the prey removed at each step gives a strictly convex cost. Using the prey density at the start of the step overestimates the catch and can create a strict local minimum with cost above the global minimum. We certify the global minimizers in a two-step example by rational root isolation. A second example shows that, with both species present and positive diffusion, a strict local minimizer for the old-state rule admits a descent direction under the flux rule. For nonnegative $H^1$ initial data and positive diffusivities in one space dimension, the two rules give costs, weighted gradients and Hessians that differ by $O(\tau)$ at the same control, uniformly in the spatial mesh. Here $\tau$ is the time step. If the old-state Hessian is uniformly coercive near a stationary control, the flux objective has a local minimizer within $O(\tau)$ of it. With uniformly bounded tracking targets, a large enough effort penalty makes both objectives strongly convex for all sufficiently small time steps. We also derive exact discrete adjoints and Hessian actions, prove a common variational limit with an IMEX discretization, and compare stationary controls across grids. The same harvest accounting applies to weighted production--destruction systems.
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Autran

item.title: The Minimal Background Period for Infinitely Many Spectral Gaps in Anderson-Bernoulli Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.22703v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider one-dimensional discrete Schr\"odinger operators with a periodic background and independent Bernoulli disorder. We ask for the least background period permitting infinitely many gaps in the almost sure spectrum. We provide explicit rational parameters at the minimum period of three, answering Wood's question. Our example gives negative answers to Bellissard's question for a disconnected background hull and to Damanik and Fillman's two finite-gap questions for transitive subshifts of finite type and subshifts of positive entropy. The proof, which appears to be new, normalizes the first background value to zero and establishes a transverse heteroclinic connection at nonzero energy. A strict scale window yields invariant multicones. For every nondegenerate Bernoulli law, gaps accumulate from the right at this spectral point. This accumulation persists under small perturbations, with its energy varying real analytically. Spectral intervals approach this point from the right, ruling out a Cantor spectrum. Three is the least background period at which exact recovery of the spectrum from periodic realizations can require unbounded fundamental periods of the total potential.

item.title: Interpolation of nonlocal Sobolev spaces for general gradients
item.description: arXiv:2611.29790v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the interpolation structure of nonlocal Sobolev spaces associated with general radial gradients. For compactly supported kernels satisfying suitable regularity and two-sided growth assumptions of fractional order, we characterize the spaces $H^{\rho,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$, $1<p<\infty$, by the Gustavsson--Peetre interpolation method between $L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $W^{1,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$. The function parameter is determined, up to equivalence, by the behavior of the kernel near the origin. We also establish a complex interpolation formula between spaces associated with different kernels and integrability exponents, in which the interpolated kernel is their geometric mean. For the corresponding nonlocal Gagliardo spaces $W^{\rho,p}(\R^n)$, defined through an integral seminorm of first differences, we prove an identification with generalized Besov spaces and a real interpolation characterization involving the same function parameter. These results extend the classical relation between Bessel potential and Gagliardo spaces beyond power-type kernels, yielding continuous embeddings between the two families and their coincidence in the Hilbertian case. We further discuss logarithmic kernels and restriction spaces on Lipschitz domains, and obtain extension and compact embedding results for the Gagliardo spaces under weaker assumptions on the kernel.
